about: Mixpanel-internal event property keys found in Mixpanel's own raw export. filterMixpanelNoise deletes every 'drop' key from event properties before import. When the source can be read twice, it first applies the source's deletes: it drops every '$delete' event, every event that a valid '$delete' in the same source deletes (backend/libquery/event_reader/delete_event_reader.cpp:137-256), and every event with '$is_deleted' true (backend/arb/reader/main.cpp:3016), then deletes every 'delete_keys' key from the events it keeps. When the source cannot be read twice, it changes no 'delete_keys' key and counts each one, and each 'watch_events' name, as seen. It counts every 'watch' key it sees, without changing it. A key moves into 'drop' with a code reference into Mixpanel's source, a sandbox reproduction, or an owner decision that the key is source-project ingestion metadata no destination wants. Evidence paths are relative to the Mixpanel analytics repo at 0bbc6a46c0e unless an entry names another commit.

drop.why: The query readers hide an event carrying it until identity management confirms the id remaps to the event's own distinct_id. That remap exists only in the source project, so in any other project the event is hidden from every query, forever. /import still counts it as imported.
drop.evidence: backend/libquery/arb_bin/reader.c:183-237; backend/libquery/brb/reader_v2/filters/global_distinct_id_filter.cpp:82-148; staging reproduction: 5,902,970 hidden events restored by re-sending without the key

delete_keys.why: Source compaction marks an event deleted with it. When deletes are applied, an event with $is_deleted true is dropped (every query hides it in the source) and the key is deleted from the rest, where it is false and does nothing.
delete_keys.evidence: backend/arb/reader/main.cpp:3016; backend/libquery/value/value.c:268-270; owner decision AK 2026-10-29 (deletes applied, analytics 7437f23a9a1)

watch_events.why: Counted only when deletes cannot be applied (the source cannot be read twice). Then a $delete event deletes the matching events in the destination, as it did in the source. When deletes are applied, every $delete event is dropped and counted in noise_removed as event:$delete.
